title: SIGA: Self-Evolving Coding-Agent Adapters for Scientific Simulation
title_zh: SIGA：用于科学仿真的自进化 Coding-Agent 适配器
abstract_en: Advanced scientific simulators expose specialized input languages that turn simulation goals into executable configurations, but learning them can cost domain scientists hours to days. We study simulator setup as a problem of agent-tool interface grounding: what minimal simulator-specific adaptations are needed for an off-the-shelf coding agent to operate real scientific software? Our intuition is that coding agents already know how to navigate files, edit code, run commands, and repair outputs, but they lack the simulator's executable contract: its vocabulary, structural constraints, validation rules, and termination conditions. We introduce SIGA, a Simulator-Interface Grounding Adapter that supplies this contract through retrieval, procedural memory, in-trajectory validation, and validation-enforced termination. We primarily evaluate SIGA on GEOS, an open-source multiphysics simulator used in subsurface science. SIGA produces a complete GEOS deck in about five minutes with TreeSim above 0.90, matching an extended-budget human expert who took about three hours, a roughly 36x wall-clock speedup. On a harder held-out set, grounding raises TreeSim from 0.720 to 0.789, a roughly 10% relative gain over the bare agent, and can reduce the across-seed standard deviation by 16x. Self-evolution further improves SIGA by rewriting adapter contents from prior trajectories, yielding the highest held-out GEOS mean and matching or outperforming the strongest hand-designed configuration. Transfers to OpenFOAM and LAMMPS show that the dominant mechanism shifts by interface: validation matters most when structural completeness is the bottleneck, while memory and retrieval matter most when domain correctness is the bottleneck. These results suggest that lightweight, self-improvable grounding layers can turn general coding agents into practical operators of scientific software.
abstract_zh: 先进科学仿真器通常提供专用输入语言，可将仿真目标转化为可执行配置，但领域科学家学习这些语言往往需要数小时到数天。本文将仿真器设置视为 agent-tool interface grounding（智能体-工具接口对齐）问题：一个现成的 coding agent 要操作真实科学软件，最少需要哪些仿真器特定适配？作者认为，coding agent 已具备文件导航、代码编辑、命令运行和输出修复能力，但缺少仿真器的“可执行契约”，包括术语词汇、结构约束、验证规则和终止条件。为此，论文提出 SIGA（Simulator-Interface Grounding Adapter），通过检索、过程记忆、轨迹内验证和验证强制终止来提供该契约。主要实验在 GEOS 这一用于地下科学的开源多物理场仿真器上进行。SIGA 可在约 5 分钟内生成完整 GEOS deck，TreeSim 超过 0.90，接近扩展预算下耗时约 3 小时的人类专家，实现约 36 倍墙钟加速。在更难的 held-out 集合上，grounding 将 TreeSim 从 0.720 提升到 0.789，相比裸 agent 约有 10% 相对增益，并可将不同随机种子的标准差降低 16 倍。自进化机制通过从既往轨迹中重写适配器内容进一步提升 SIGA，在 held-out GEOS 上取得最高均值，并达到或超过最强手工设计配置。迁移到 OpenFOAM 和 LAMMPS 的结果表明，不同接口下主导机制不同：当结构完整性是瓶颈时，验证最关键；当领域正确性是瓶颈时，记忆和检索更关键。这些结果说明，轻量且可自我改进的 grounding 层可以将通用 coding agent 转化为实用的科学软件操作员。
key_points_zh: 论文将科学仿真器配置生成建模为 agent-tool interface grounding 问题，核心是为通用 coding agent 补足仿真器的可执行契约，而非重新训练模型。
SIGA 由检索、过程记忆、轨迹内验证和验证强制终止组成，帮助 agent 理解 GEOS 等仿真器的词汇、结构约束、验证规则与完成条件。
在 GEOS 上，SIGA 约 5 分钟生成完整 deck，TreeSim 超过 0.90，接近耗时约 3 小时的人类专家，实现约 36 倍墙钟加速。
在更难 held-out 集上，SIGA 将 TreeSim 从裸 agent 的 0.720 提升到 0.789，并显著降低跨随机种子的性能波动；自进化版本进一步达到最佳均值。
跨 OpenFOAM 和 LAMMPS 的迁移实验显示，不同仿真器接口的关键瓶颈不同：结构完整性依赖验证，领域正确性更依赖记忆与检索。

llm_assessment.comment: A strong adapter-based harness contribution with validation, procedural memory, and trajectory-based self-evolution for scientific software agents.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 该工作通过验证、程序性记忆和轨迹驱动自演化构建科学软件代理适配层，是较强的 harness 贡献。
